concept.name: Yield farming
concept.definition: Yield farming is the practice of deploying crypto assets across DeFi protocols — lending pools, liquidity pools, staking — to maximize returns from interest, trading fees and token incentives, often moving capital frequently to chase the highest rates.
concept.intuition: It is rate-chasing on steroids: farmers shuttle capital to wherever the combination of fees, interest and reward tokens pays the most this week.
concept.mechanics: Farmers supply liquidity or collateral to protocols and harvest multiple income streams: base yield (fees/interest) plus incentive token emissions. Strategies include leveraged looping (deposit, borrow, redeposit) and auto-compounding vaults; net return must be weighed against gas costs, impermanent loss, reward-token price decay and smart contract risk.
concept.formula: Net farm PnL = fees + interest + reward token value − impermanent loss − gas − borrow costs.
concept.failure_modes: Advertised APYs assume reward tokens hold value — emissions-driven yields collapse when the token dumps; unaudited farms are frequent rug/exploit targets, and leveraged loops liquidate catastrophically in drawdowns.
concept.misconceptions: Triple-digit APYs are not sustainable yield — they are mostly marketing paid in inflationary tokens whose sell pressure the farmer joins. 'Auto-compounding' compounds losses just as reliably when the underlying position deteriorates.
concept.example: A farmer deposits stETH as Aave collateral, borrows ETH at 2.5%, swaps to stETH and redeposits, looping to ~3x a 2.9% staking yield — until a stETH depeg forces liquidation of the whole stack.
